'''Yakir Aharonov''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|ForMemRS}} ({{langx|he|יקיר אהרונוב}}; born August 28, 1932)<ref name="AharonovCU">{{cite web|url=http://www.chapman.edu/our-faculty/yakir-aharonov|title=Yakir Aharonov's Homepage at Chapman University|publisher=Chapman University|access-date=February 17, 2013|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130118055409/http://www.chapman.edu/our-faculty/yakir-aharonov|archive-date=January 18, 2013}}</ref> is an [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[physicist]] specializing in [[quantum physics]]. He has been a Professor of Theoretical Physics and the James J. Farley Professor of Natural Philosophy at [[Chapman University]] in California since 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite encyclopedia |year=2007 |title=AHARONOV, YAKIR (1932–) |encyclopedia=[[Encyclopaedia Judaica]] |publisher=Thomson Gale |location= |last=Seckbach |first=Fern Lee |edition=2nd |volume=1 |page=537 |isbn=978-0-02-865929-9 |last2=Rossing |first2=Ruth}}</ref> He was a distinguished professor in the [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics|Perimeter Institute]] between 2009-2012<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/News/In_The_Media/Nine_Leading_Researchers_Join_Stephen_Hawking_as_Distinguished_Research_Chairs_at_PI/|title=Nine Leading Researchers Join Stephen Hawking as Distinguished Research Chairs at PI - Perimeter Institute|website=www.perimeterinstitute.ca|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121031162222/http://www.perimeterinstitute.ca/News/In_The_Media/Nine_Leading_Researchers_Join_Stephen_Hawking_as_Distinguished_Research_Chairs_at_PI/|archive-date=31 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Aharonov, Yakir, 1932- |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11408012.html |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=history.aip.org}}</ref> and is a professor emeritus at [[Tel Aviv University]] and at [[University of South Carolina]]. He is president of the IYAR, the Israeli Institute for Advanced Research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iyar.org.il/about-6.html|title=אייר - המכון הישראלי למחקר מתקדם - סגל המכון|website=www.iyar.org.il|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301225130/http://www.iyar.org.il/about-6.html|archive-date=1 March 2018}}</ref> 

In June 2024 he was elected to serve in the [[Royal Society]] of London.<ref>{{Cite news |last=ynet |last2=ynet |date=2024-06-09 |title=בלונדון ובציריך: הישגים לשני פרופסורים מאוניברסיטת ת"א |url=https://www.ynet.co.il/environment-science/article/b1oq2tfr0 |access-date=2025-12-18 |work=Ynet |language=he}}</ref>

==Biography==
Yakir Aharonov was born in [[Haifa]]. He received his undergraduate education at the [[Technion – Israel Institute of Technology]] in [[Haifa]], graduating with a [[BSc]] in 1956. He continued his graduate studies at the Technion and then moved to [[Bristol University|Bristol University, UK]] together with his doctoral advisor [[David Bohm]], receiving a [[PhD|Ph.D.]] degree in 1960. Aharonov later taught at [[Brandeis University]] from 1960 to 1961 and the [[Yeshiva University]] from 1964 to 1967, both in the [[United States]].<ref name=":0" />

Aharonov is married to Nily, an educational psychologist, and has two children. His brother, [[Dov Aharonov]], is a professor emeritus at the Faculty of Mathematics at the [[Technion]], and his niece, [[Dorit Aharonov]], is a professor at the School of Engineering and Computer Science at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

==Academic career==
Aharonov's research interests are [[quantum field theory|quantum field theories]], nonlocal and topological effects in [[quantum mechanics]], and interpretations of [[quantum mechanics]]. In 1959, he and [[David Bohm]] proposed the [[Aharonov–Bohm effect]]<ref name="Significance of electromagnetic potentials in quantum theory">{{cite journal |author=Aharonov, Y |author2=Bohm, D |date=1959 |title=Significance of electromagnetic potentials in quantum theory |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=115 |issue=3 |pages=485–491 |bibcode=1959PhRv..115..485A |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.115.485 |doi-access=free}}</ref> for which he co-received the 1998 [[Wolf Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-12-10 |title=Yakir Aharonov |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2018/12/10/yakir-aharonov/ |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-05-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531090918/https://wolffund.org.il/2018/12/10/yakir-aharonov/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 1988, Aharonov, [[David Albert]], and [[Lev Vaidman]]  published their theory of [[weak value]]s.<ref name="Aharonov1988">{{cite journal
 | author = Yakir Aharonov | author2=David Z. Albert |author3=Lev Vaidman
 | title = How the result of a measurement of a component of the spin of a spin-1/2 particle can turn out to be 100
 | journal = Physical Review Letters
 | volume = 60
 | issue = 14
 | pages = 1351–1354
 | year = 1988
 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.1351
 | bibcode = 1988PhRvL..60.1351A
 | pmid=10038016}}</ref> This work was motivated by Aharonov's long-time quest to experimentally verify his theory that events in quantum mechanics that appear to be random are caused by events in the future ([[two-state vector formalism]]). Verifying a present effect of a future cause requires a measurement, and that would ordinarily destroy coherence and ruin the experiment. He and his colleagues claim that they were able to use [[weak measurement]]s and verify the present effect of a future cause.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-08-03 |title=Can the future affect the past? |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/can-the-future-affect-the-past/ |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref> Working with Aharon Casher, they predicted the [[Aharonov–Casher effect]], the electrodynamic dual of the Aharonov–Bohm effect with magnetic dipoles and charges.<ref name=":0" />

===Timeline===
*1960–1961: Research Associate, [[Brandeis University]]
*1961–1964: Assistant Professor, Yeshiva University
*1964–1967: Associate Professor, Yeshiva University
*1967–1973: Joint professorship at Tel Aviv University and [[Yeshiva University]]
*1973–2006: Joint professorship at Tel Aviv University and the [[University of South Carolina]]
*2006–2008: Professor at [[George Mason University]]
*2008–present: Professor of Theoretical Physics and the James J. Farley Professor of Natural Philosophy at [[Chapman University]]

==Awards and recognition==
*1978: Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1978&unit_id=&institution=Tel+Aviv+University|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311202006/http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1978&unit_id=&institution=Tel+Aviv+University|archive-date=11 March 2018}}</ref>
*1984: [[Weizmann Prize for Research in the Exact Sciences|Weizmann Prize]] in Physics
*1984: Rothschild Prize in Physics<ref name=":0" />
*1989: [[Israel Prize]] in exact science<ref name=prize>{{Cite web| title = Israel Prize Official Site – Recipients in 1989 (in Hebrew)| url = http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashmag/Tashnab_Tashmag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashmat| url-status = live| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120307204755/http://cms.education.gov.il/EducationCMS/Units/PrasIsrael/Tashmag/Tashnab_Tashmag_Rikuz.htm?DictionaryKey=Tashmat| archive-date = 2012-03-07}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
*1990: Elected to the [[Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]
*1991: [[The Franklin Institute Awards|The Elliott Cresson Medal]] – [[The Franklin Institute]]<ref name=":0" />
*1992: Honorary Doctor of Science, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
*1993: Elected Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]], USA
*1993: Honorary Doctor of Science, University of South Carolina, USA
*1995: Hewlett–Packard Europhysics Prize
*1997: Honorary Doctor of Science, Bristol University, UK
*1998: [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] with [[Michael Berry (physicist)|Michael Berry]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=25&cat_title=PHYSICS|title=תוצאות חיפוש|last=Simply-Smart|website=www.wolffund.org.il|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205055435/http://www.wolffund.org.il/cat.asp?id=25&cat_title=PHYSICS|archive-date=5 February 2012}}</ref><ref name=":0" />
*1999: Honorary Doctor of Science, University of Buenos Aires, Argentina
*2009: Selected [[List of Clarivate Citation laureates in Physics|Clarivate Citation laureate in Physics]] with Michael Berry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thomson Reuters Predicts Nobel Laureates |url=https://www.newswire.ca/content/newswire-ca/ca/en/news-releases.detail.html/null.htm |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=www.newswire.ca |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230712120058/https://www.newswire.ca/content/newswire-ca/ca/en/news-releases.detail.html/null.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*2006: [[EMET Prize]] in [[Exact Science]]
*In 2009, the information service [[Thomson Reuters]] named Aharonov as leading candidate for the 2009 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]], based on his work's influence on quantum physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://science.thomsonreuters.com/nobel/nominees/#physics|title=ScienceWatch.com - Clarivate Analytics|first=Clarivate|last=Analytics|website=science.thomsonreuters.com|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100810014609/http://science.thomsonreuters.com/nobel/nominees/#physics|archive-date=10 August 2010}}</ref>
*2010: [[National Medal of Science]] (2009), awarded and presented by President [[Barack Obama]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalacademies.org/headlines/20101018.html|title=National-Academies.org - Winners of National Medals of Science, Technology Announced|website=www.nationalacademies.org|access-date=7 May 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101020140032/http://www.nationalacademies.org/headlines/20101018.html|archive-date=20 October 2010}}</ref>
*2024: Foreign Member of the Royal Society<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Yakir Aharonov ForMemRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/yakir-aharonov-36776/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
